In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the energy spectra obtained by GAMMA are in a good agreement with the results of the balloon experiments in the energy range 10 3–10 4 TeV.
the energy spectra of cosmic rays obtained by the GAM-Ma experiment in the knee region are in a good agreement with those obtained by other experiments in the same energy range.

the knee is not a single feature but a complex phenomenon, with several components, which is a manifestation of the interplay of the different physical mechanisms that are responsible for the production of cosmic rays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the possibility to determine the primary energy spectrum and the elemental composition of cosmic rays in the energy range 10 3–10 5 Te V with the help of the GAMMA experiment.
the EAS data of the GAMMA experiment are in a good agreement with the extrapolations of the direct measurements of the primary cosmic ray fluxes to energies above 10 3 GeV.

the GAMMA experiment has shown that the energy spectrum in the knee region is a function of the rigidity of the primary cosmic ray and that the energy of the knee depends on the rigidity of primary cosmic ray.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the knee in the cosmic ray spectrum is caused by the rigidity dependent cut-off of the primary spectrum.
the knee feature is not an artefact of a particular interaction model or of the reconstruction method.
the energy spectra and composition of cosmic rays can be derived with a high level of reliability in the knee region using the EAS inverse approach and the SIBYL and QGSJETS interaction models.
